question: After auditing the CDF certificate, can the same Poisson corrector give a separately checkable mean first-passage certificate and an exponential tail bound?

literature_before_freeze.source: Meyn and Tweedie 1993, Stability of Markovian Processes III
literature_before_freeze.actually_read: Section 1.3 and Theorem 1.1; CD2 and Theorem 4.3(i), including proof; finite-matrix argument will be supplied separately
prior original unit plus current reread of backward equation argument; reversible theorem not applied to killed model

conditions: all previous finite homogeneous block assumptions
planned_claims: mean relative error bounded by endpoint intervals relative to z
with cstar=max(abs(c_i)/z_i), rstar=max(abs(r_i)), sufficient 1% threshold nu>=rstar+100*(cstar+rstar), when cstar+rstar>0; exact mean if both zero
validation: A: NumPy/SciPy builds matrices and solves independently from frozen model; no old helper imports
B: standard-library Fraction, analytic two-state H, Cramer determinant linear solves; no NumPy/SciPy
Exact full mean by 4x4 first-step equations checks interval endpoints; six model-speed pairs only
Keep failures when v or g not positive; failure is uncertified, not infinite true mean
No CDF grid or 776-point rerun; no Monte Carlo
Verify exact residual and interval mean bounds; float relative tolerance 1e-10
logical_counterexample: Use the already-described mixed exponential example only to explain non-implication, without relabeling it as a new finding or a counterexample to the fixed K,L theorem.
retention: All six pairs, including rejection cases; no choosing parameters after observing results
novelty: unestablished; standard Poisson/Lyapunov comparison adapted to this small tutorial
